paper.title_en: Precision Spectroscopy of the Fine and Hyperfine Structures of High Molecular Rydberg-Stark States: Metrology of Molecular Hydrogen Ions
paper.abstract_en: The Stark effect in autoionizing high-<math display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math> Rydberg states decouples the Rydberg electron from the ion core through <math display="inline"><mrow><mo>ℓ</mo></mrow></math> mixing with core-nonpenetrating high-<math display="inline"><mo>ℓ</mo></math> states. The Rydberg states become long-lived, which is ideal for precision spectroscopy, and their structures reflect the fine and hyperfine structures of the ion-core levels. We report on precision measurements, in weak electric fields, of the fine and hyperfine structures of two distinct categories of high autoionizing molecular Rydberg-Stark states differing by the nature of the ion-core angular momentum: Rydberg states of para-<math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> (total nuclear spin <math display="inline"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>,</mn><mn>2</mn></math>) with a rotationally excited (<math display="inline"><msup><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>) <math display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> ion core and Rydberg states of ortho-<math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> (<math display="inline"><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>) with a rotationless (<math display="inline"><msup><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>) ion core. The spectra reveal striking differences which are interpreted as arising from the dominance of anisotropic charge-quadrupole interactions between the rotating quadrupolar ion core and the Rydberg electron in para-<math display="inline"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and the absence of such interactions in rotationless ortho-<math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> Rydberg states. In ortho-<math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, the dominant interaction, the magnetic Fermi-contact hyperfine interaction in the ion core, does not significantly affect the motion of the Rydberg electron. By analyzing these spectra based on a treatment combining multichannel quantum-defect theory and matrix diagonalization, we derive new experimental values of the hyperfine coupling constant <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>139.84</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>MHz</mi></mrow></math> of <math display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the spin-rotation coupling constant <math display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>39.62</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>MHz</mi></mrow></math> of <math display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and the fundamental vibrational interval of ortho-<math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> [47 279 980.8(1.9) MHz]. The approach followed here in the study of molecular Rydberg-Stark states is general and broadly applicable to measurements of the fine and hyperfine structures of molecular cations.
